Blend lime and orange juice, fish stock, chilli, coriander and salt.
Add the olive oil at the end of blending.
Keep at 0–4 °C; pour 45 g per portion at service. The orange softens the acidity for oily fish.
844b4667.st: Leche de tigre: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Not suitable for freezing.

c: Dissolve sugar in boiling water; cool slightly.
Chop mint finely (do not blend); add to the syrup with vinegar and salt.
Rest 30 min; serve at room temperature with roast lamb.

Squeeze out the flesh (≈ 25 g) and mash to a paste.
Pulse the olives in a food processor to a coarse paste (or chop finely).
Add capers, anchovies and the roasted garlic paste.
Add the olive oil gradually to a spreadable consistency.
Finish with thyme, lemon zest and black pepper. No added salt – olives, capers and anchovies season the tapenade.
Store covered with a thin layer of olive oil.
314d131b.st: Tapenade: 0–4 °C, 5 days, closed container, surface covered with oil. Not suitable for freezing.

c: Finely dice the tomatoes; chop the olives and capers.
Combine with the shallot, garlic, parsley and dill.
Add the lemon zest, juice and olive oil; mix gently.
Season with pepper; add salt only if needed (olives and capers are salty).
Spoon 50 g over hot trout immediately before service.
d304ff5c.al: None of the 14 declared allergens. Olives, capers: check label (14 Sulphites).

c: Sweat the onion in the oil until completely soft, without colour, 8–10 min.
Add the tomato paste; cook 1–2 min.
Add the flour; cook 2–3 min, stirring.
Off the heat, stir in the paprikas and cayenne at once so they do not burn.
Whisk in the hot stock gradually, then the passata.
Blend completely smooth; add the vinegar, sugar and salt.
Pass through a fine sieve; adjust the consistency with a little hot stock if needed.
Hot hold ≥63 °C, or chill to ≤4 °C within 90 min.

c: Blend the peeled roasted pepper to a smooth purée.
Sweat the finely diced onion in the oil over medium heat until translucent.
Add the tomatoes and pepper purée; simmer 10 min.
Add the spices, sugar, salt and pepper; simmer gently 20–25 min until slightly thickened.
Off the heat, add the chopped cilantro and parsley; blend smooth or leave slightly textured.
Check the seasoning; chill to ≤4 °C within 90 min.
2eb49477.st: 0–4 °C, 5 days in a sealed container; −18 °C, 3 months.

c: Simmer the plums with the water for 15–20 min until very soft.
Blend smooth; pass through a fine sieve.
Return to the pan; add the garlic, chili, coriander, khmeli-suneli, sugar and salt.
Simmer on low heat 10–15 min to a light coating consistency.
Add the vinegar; adjust sugar and vinegar to the acidity of the plums.
Stir in the chopped cilantro, dill and mint for the last minute.
c3dc22a7.al: None of the 14 declared allergens. Vinegar: check label (14 Sulphites).

Finely chop the olives, capers, shallot and parsley; cut the basil in chiffonade.
Mash the garlic confit (stored at 0–4 °C) and whisk with the oil, lemon juice, mustard, zest, salt and pepper.
Fold the dressing into the tomato mixture.
Check the seasoning; chill at 0–4 °C for 20–30 min.
Serve chilled or at room temperature (max. 2 h out of refrigeration).
60ffab40.st: 0–4 °C, 48 h in an airtight container. Do not freeze.

c: Roast red peppers at 220 °C convection 25–30 min, peel, deseed and purée (or use ready purée).
Blend all ingredients to a smooth texture.

Melt the sugar over medium heat to a light golden caramel.
Add the butter and stir until smooth.
Add the apples, water and lemon juice; bring to the boil, then simmer 12–15 min until soft.
Blend until smooth and pass through a fine sieve.
Finish with the cinnamon and vanilla.
Serve warm (hold at 63 °C or above) or cool to below 5 °C within 90 min.
Serve 50 g per portion with duck, pork, roast poultry or desserts.
Rest at 0–4 °C for at least 1 h to develop the smoky flavour.
Heat the oil in a saucepan; fry the garlic and ginger lightly until fragrant.
Add the sugar, honey, soy sauce, lemon and orange juice; stir and bring to the boil.
Boil 3–4 min until the sugar has dissolved.
Slake the cornflour in the cold water; add in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook 2–3 min more until thick, smooth and glossy.
Cool to below 5 °C within 90 min, or hold at 63 °C or above for warm service.
Serve 40 g per portion with fish, duck, salads or seafood.
Warm the honey over low heat; do not boil.
Add the soy sauce, sriracha and vinegar; stir and simmer gently at 85–90 °C for 2–3 min.
Strain for a smooth glaze, or leave the garlic in for a stronger flavour.
Use to glaze chicken wings, ribs or vegetables in the last minutes of cooking.
Chill unused glaze to ≤4 °C within 90 min.

Heat 5 min over medium heat, stirring, until thickened and lightly caramelised.
Use warm as a glaze, or cool to below 5 °C within 90 min.

Reserve 15 g of the sugar and mix it with the agar-agar.
Cook the fruit, vegetables, remaining sugar, salt and coriander over low heat for 25–30 min until completely soft.
Blend completely smooth; pass through a fine sieve.
Whisk the agar-sugar mix into about 150 g of the warm sauce, then combine with the rest.
Bring to a full boil, stirring; boil 1–2 min to hydrate the agar.
Off the heat, add the lime juice; blend briefly.
Chill to ≤4 °C within 90 min; transfer to a clean container or squeeze bottle.

Roast whole red peppers in a convection oven at 220 °C for 20–25 min until charred; cover 10 min, then peel and deseed (≈280 g raw gives 180 g).
Sauté the garlic and chilies in 15 g of the olive oil for 1–2 min without colour.
Blend all ingredients until completely smooth and emulsified.
Chill to ≤4 °C and rest 12–24 h before use.

c: Mix soy sauce, honey, ginger and garlic in a small saucepan.
Warm gently to 70 °C until the honey dissolves; do not boil.
Off the heat, add lime juice and sesame oil. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Blitz deseeded chilli (keep some seeds for heat) and garlic coarsely.
Boil sugar, vinegar, water and salt; add chilli and garlic, simmer 5 min.
Thicken with corn starch slurry; boil 1 min; cool (thickens on cooling).
Serve with spring rolls, fish cakes, fried chicken.

c: Wrap whole beetroot in foil; roast in a convection oven at 180 °C for 50–60 min until tender. Cool, peel and weigh.
Blend the beetroot with the orange juice on high speed until smooth.
Add the balsamic vinegar and olive oil; blend to a velvety texture. Season with the salt.
Pass through a fine sieve. Cool to below 5 °C within 90 min; keep in a squeeze bottle at 0–4 °C.
Use as a plating sauce, 15 g per plate.

Blend all ingredients to a smooth cream.
Taste for salt and acidity; transfer to a container, cover the surface with film and chill at 0–4 °C.
ba175968.st: Avocado sauce: 0–4 °C, 24 h, surface covered with film to prevent browning; −18 °C, 1 month.

c: Blanch the peas in boiling salted water 3–4 min; refresh at once in iced water to keep the colour. Drain well.
Blend the peas with the warm cream on high speed until smooth; emulsify in the olive oil until glossy. Season with the salt.
Pass through a fine sieve. Cool to below 5 °C within 90 min; keep in a squeeze bottle at 0–4 °C.
Use as a plating sauce, 15 g per plate (dots or swipe).

Blend with butter and cream to a smooth purée.
Pass through a fine sieve for a silky texture.
Season with salt and white pepper.
For service, heat to 75 °C core and serve warm; hold at ≥ 63 °C max. 1 h to keep the colour.
Roast pumpkin wedges in a convection oven at 180 °C for 35–40 min until soft and lightly coloured. Scoop out the flesh and weigh.
Blend the pumpkin with the warm cream, honey, salt and nutmeg until smooth and creamy.
Pass through a fine sieve. Cool to below 5 °C within 90 min; keep in a squeeze bottle at 0–4 °C.
Use as a plating sauce, 15 g per plate.

Blend all ingredients until smooth; taste for salt.
Chill at 0–4 °C, surface covered with film.

Add the tomato paste; cook 1–2 min.
Add the passata and stock; bring to a simmer.
Add the basil, oregano, salt, pepper and the sugar (adjust to the acidity of the tomatoes).
Blend smooth, or leave slightly rustic as required.
